description: Eval scenarios for the pkg-skills plugin. Run each query against a session with the plugin installed; expected_behavior is the grading rubric. Test across Haiku, Sonnet, and Opus.

scenarios.query: Index the packages installed on my system and show me which ones could get skills. Then run the sync again and confirm nothing changed.
expected_behavior: Runs `pkg-skills sync` (or bun fallback) rather than enumerating managers manually
Reports the package count and that new entries are commented out (not opted in)
Second sync produces a byte-identical packages.conf and the agent states it is idempotent
Does not edit packages.conf opt-in state without being asked

scenarios.query: Opt ripgrep in and generate its skill, then prove the result follows Anthropic skill best practices.
expected_behavior: Uncomments pacman:ripgrep in packages.conf (or instructs pkg-skills select), then runs `pkg-skills generate ripgrep`
Resulting skill is named pkg-ripgrep with cheatsheet, commands, references (cli-help/man/reference/links), examples, snippets, scripts/sync.sh, meta.json
Runs `pkg-skills validate` on the output and reports zero errors
SKILL.md description is third person with the use case first; body links bundled files one level deep
Uses the injected meta JSON and template blueprints from the command's dynamic context — does not re-fetch docs from the network
Substitutes ${VAR} placeholders and resolves @ref lines by reading the cache dir from CACHE_DIR
Improves prose beyond the deterministic output: real task->command cheatsheet rows and examples using actual rg flags, keeping $ARGUMENTS/@FILENAME parameterization
Validates with `pkg-skills validate` and installs with `skills add` only after zero errors

scenarios.query: Set things up so skills regenerate automatically whenever I install or update a package.
expected_behavior: Runs `pkg-skills units install` and relays the printed sudo commands for the alpm hook instead of running them unprompted
Enables pkg-skills.timer and pkg-skills-drain.path with systemctl --user
Explains the spool/drain bridge and the trade-off that cargo/bun/npm changes are caught by the daily timer, not instantly
